payload.acceptance_criteria:
The kit finds the mail root from a main checkout, a linked worktree with an absolute or relative gitdir, and a submodule, with no subprocess.
A version 2 lock owner file records name, time, note, process id and process start time.
The version 1 agent-mail code reads a version 2 lock as held, and the kit reads a version 1 lock as held with unknown liveness.
A lock whose process is not alive is reported as stale by name and is released only by an explicit repair command.
payload.description:
## Context
The agent-mail scripts move into the kit, but three behaviours change: the mail root is found by reading the .git file instead of running git, the kit spawns no process, and the lock owner file gains the process id and its start time so stale locks and the role lock can be checked for liveness. Old and new code must read each other's locks during migration.
payload.requirements: No vendor credential is collected, stored or brokered (requirement R0 of basicly-qpr2xmr).
payload.title: Orchestrator kit: store and lock format version 2

payload.acceptance_criteria:
In a scratch mail root, a message sent by either tool is listed, read and marked read by the other.
A lock taken by either tool is refused to the other with exit code 3, and only the holder or an explicit break releases it.
who, status, wait and log of both tools show the same state.
payload.description:
## Context
A workspace may run an older shell mail script beside the Python agent-mail scripts. Migration assumes that no mail moves, which holds only if each tool reads the other's mailboxes and locks.

## Context
An idle session keeps one blocking orch wait running so that the model spends no tokens until mail arrives. Whether a background or long-running wait keeps each vendor's session from going idle and wakes it on mail, and what one empty wake cycle costs in tokens, is pending probe P8.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
For each vendor and each normal ask mode, a scratch ask rule on a harmless command is recorded as prompting or not, before and after a don't-ask-again answer.
The list of modes that skip ask rules is taken from current vendor documentation and tested against recorded hook input only.
payload.description:
## Context
orch approve may run only under the vendor's own ask prompt, so the owner sees the full command. Whether an ask rule always shows the prompt in the normal ask modes, also after an answer of don't ask again, is pending probe P6. Modes that skip ask rules are never run; the kit refuses them from recorded hook input. The probe runs last, in a scratch project with project-level settings.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
docs/design holds the orchestrator kit design draft 4 and states where a consumer with no engine gets the capability.
Every vendor fact in it names its source or the probe that will establish it.
It contains no machine path, user name, host name or private session name.
payload.description:
## Context
The kit's design lives in a private working copy. Draft 4 is its public form in docs/design: written for a public reader with no private paths, names or quotes, vendor facts marked pending their probe, and the review findings applied: approvals bind to the diff hash and the named path blobs, to HEAD only for a push; the moved mail scripts list their behaviour changes; P10 and P11 are probes; context lines are rate-limited; tests use an injected clock.
payload.requirements: No vendor credential is collected, stored or brokered (requirement R0 of basicly-qpr2xmr).
payload.title: Orchestrator kit: design document draft 4

payload.text: Orchestrator kit: one protocol for sessions on Claude Code, Codex CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI: mailboxes and locks moved from the agent-mail skill, one orchestrator role lock, approval records bound to an exact action, and vendor adapters for hooks. It ships in basicly like the tracker kit; a consumer with no engine installs the basicly-orch package. Approvals are off by default and are mistake-proofing and audit, not a security control. Landing waits for basicly-5zqycyb (Windows and macOS proof of the agent-mail scripts). Tasks: the records titled Orchestrator kit under this feature.
The Orchestrator kit tasks under basicly-qpr2xmr.3 deliver the cross-vendor messaging and approval layer of this meta harness as a basicly kit; its requirement R0 holds for the kit.

Probe P10 result 2026-11-17: passed in a scratch mail root on copies of a shell mail script and the agent-mail Python scripts. A message sent by either tool was peeked, read and marked read by the other. A lock taken by either tool was refused to the other with exit 3, a non-holder unlock was refused with exit 1, and the Python unlock --break released a shell lock. who, status, wait (exit 0 on mail) and log showed the same state. Differences: the shell tool has no --break, each hint names its own command, and the Python tool needs the agent-mail-root marker. Consequence: migration needs no mail move. The probe script is to be committed with the design lane so the check can run again.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When another session lands a claim on the record while this claim's push is blocked, and the win takes more than one second, this claim answers exit 3 LOST and names the winning session as holder.
payload.description:
## Context
When another session wins a record while my claim's push is blocked, I want my claim to answer LOST and name the holder, so an agent knows at once who holds the record.

## Finding
2026-11-17. tests/test_kit_vault_claim_joined_owner.py::test_a_claim_stops_retrying_its_share_after_fetching_another_winner failed in a landing verify at load 22. Deterministic reproduction: add time.sleep(1.5) before the winner's claim. The follower then answers {exit: 4, unsettled: 'the vault refused the share 1 times; 1 events stay queued; run sync again'} instead of exit 3 LOST with holder winner, 3 of 3 runs, with claim_s 0.143. Pausing the follower's ticks and Ask clock while its push is blocked does not change it, so the follower's own deadline is not the cause. Safe (nothing lost, next commands named) but the answer is wrong. Cause unknown at filing. Blocks the 0.46.3 release under basicly-gtb19bg.43.42.
payload.title: Answer LOST with the holder when another session wins while this claim's push is blocked

payload.text: [2026-11-17 root cause, basicly session] Not a wrong answer. Logging every git call: in the slow case the follower's push is held by the test past its 1 s deadline; vault_share.share measured its budget with time.monotonic, not the claim's clock, so it ends at its deadline without the final fetch and the claim answers 4. That is the deadline contract working. The defect was that the claim's injected clock never reached the share, so the test could not control it. Fixed in lane claude-eight-retry, commit 86275f71: claim passes clock=budget.now to share (production default unchanged). Controls: delayed winner gives LOST, follower's own overrun gives 4, old kit with delayed winner gives 4. Recommend closing this record as not a product defect once 86275f71 lands.

[2026-11-17] Third test of this class: test_a_claim_stops_retrying_its_share_after_fetching_another_winner (deadline=1 with a threaded winner). Fixed by passing the claim clock to the share (86275f71) and pausing the follower clock while the test holds its push. The two tests named above remain.
